title: Wrap Rust string-utils functions in a TextAnalyzer struct
description: A Rust string-utils library has standalone functions. Wrap them in a TextAnalyzer struct so callers can chain operations on a text value.

task_spec.prompt:
The Rust library in src/lib.rs has word_count(s: &str) -> usize and capitalize_words(s: &str) -> String as free functions. Add a TextAnalyzer struct that wraps these:

pub struct TextAnalyzer<'a> {
    text: &'a str,
}

impl<'a> TextAnalyzer<'a> {
    pub fn new(text: &'a str) -> Self
    pub fn word_count(&self) -> usize        // delegates to the free function
    pub fn capitalize(&self) -> String       // delegates to the free function
}

The free functions must stay exactly as they are — do not modify them.

Write 3 tests for TextAnalyzer:
  test_analyzer_word_count — TextAnalyzer::new("hello world").word_count() == 2
  test_analyzer_capitalize — TextAnalyzer::new("hello world").capitalize() == "Hello World"
  test_analyzer_empty — TextAnalyzer::new("").word_count() == 0

All 3 original tests must still pass. cargo test must pass all 6 tests. cargo build must succeed.
required_artifacts: pub struct TextAnalyzer<'a> with new, word_count, and capitalize methods
success_criteria: TextAnalyzer delegates to existing free functions
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `cargo test` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
